size_grade:
UNDERESTIMATE, but in the right TIER — it is Standard, not Micro, and the report is correct about that. The 250-320 production lines / ~150 test lines is roughly 60-70% of what this will actually take, for four reasons the report did not price: (1) FIVE CharacterSheetView builders must each be given a `radar` value, not the two named — creatureSheet, defenderSheet, structureSheet, castleSheet and the unmentioned stinkCloudSheet, each with its own justification docblock in this repo's house style; (2) `rosterAxisMaxima()` is four field mappings plus a null guard across two differently-shaped config tables (CREATURE_CONFIGS' `maxAccel`/`hp`/`def` vs DEFENDER_CONFIGS' `moveAccel`/`unitStats: {hp,def} | null`), not the one-line reduce the signature implies; (3) `radarBand` must be tested against FIVE distinct label/derived sets, not the two the report lists — the ordinary creature, the zombie boss with its 18-char 'ROT' derived, the emitter tower, the shooting tower with the AURA row, the stink bag and the 268-wide castle; (4) this codebase's docblock convention means every ruling, every MINE-not-his number (the 6% visible floor, the axis choice, the maxima derivation) carries a paragraph with its measurement, and that is real line count — `characterSheetModel.ts` is 1503 lines of which the majority is prose.

Realistic figure: 400-550 lines across one new production file, one new test file, two edited production files and two edited test files. Still ONE session, still comfortably inside Standard, but the brief should say 400-550 so the branch does not treat the last third as scope creep and start cutting the tests. The report's best instinct is its scope-discipline line — *"do ONLY this: add the radar. Do not refactor the sheet, do not tidy the duplicated PAD/PORTRAIT/ROW_H constants, do not touch the stat rows"* — and that should be copied into the brief verbatim, because S182's defect-per-round count tracked how much each session changed rather than how hard the task was. Keeping the duplicated constants at characterSheetModel.ts:325-329 / characterSheet.ts:50-53 as a KNOWN, DELIBERATE non-fix is exactly right.
net_assessment:
THE REPORT IS GOOD AND IT IS NOT A VERDICT. Its structural findings are real and I could not break them: the empty band exists exactly where the owner pointed, its geometry is derivable from shipped constants, the four axes are already in hand at the call site, the feature is render-only and costs no protocol bump, the art cost is genuinely zero with three shipped Pixi precedents, and its single best catch — that `STAT_POINT_MAX` 12 must NOT be the axis max or every boss clips off the top and Vlad reads like a mid unit — would have saved the branch from shipping the opposite of what the owner asked for. Fifteen of seventeen evidence entries survive at CONFIRMED or PARTIAL.

BUT THE DESIGN RECOMMENDATION IS WHERE IT BREAKS, AND IT BREAKS ON THE OWNER'S OWN EXAMPLE. The report rejects ATTACK SPEED because two table entries are fabrications, then recommends RANGE in its place. RANGE is worse on both counts. It is FLAT AT 35 across all six tier-9 bosses and all six tier-3 units — `makeT9BossConfig` and `makeT3Config` both hard-set `attackRange: GOBLIN_ATTACK_RANGE` (voltkin-config.ts:916 and :849, constant at constants.ts:3163) — so a bat and Vlad, the literal pair he described, are IDENTICAL on it. And it carries three liars, not the two it rejected attack-speed for: Helga's 380 is a documented chase leash, the drone's 110 is a blast radius, the sapper's 70 is a blast radius. Combine that with SPEED, where the bat's 168 BEATS Vlad's 133, and the recommended six-axis chart gives Vlad a huge hull on four axes and a WEAKER-OR-EQUAL reading than a level-one bat on both of the two the report added. That is not "mega developed"; it is the effect he asked for, diluted by the two axes this report chose. The report flags the boss-speed wrinkle honestly but never states this consequence, and it is the thing most likely to make him say it is wrong.

THREE OMISSIONS THAT COST THE BRANCH TIME RATHER THAN CORRECTNESS: a fifth CharacterSheetView constructor (`stinkCloudSheet`) that tsc will force and the brief leaves blank; the zombie boss's fifth 'ROT' row whose 18-character derived string is the longest in the game and roughly halves the band on one of the six bosses this feature exists for; and `characterSheetMirror.test.ts`, which already deep-equals the whole view across the wire and would guard the new field for free — the most valuable test in the repo for this change, unnamed in a section titled tests_owed. One citation is REFUTED outright (voltkin-config.ts:205/:180 — the field is at :322 and the docblock at :297) and four more drift by one to two lines; the substance holds in every case, but under this lane's own rule that is the S120 pattern in miniature and the brief must carry corrected coordinates.

WHAT I WOULD TELL THE BRANCH. Build it — the lane is sound, the cost is zero, the determinism verdict survives, and no canon ruling is threatened (checked: `canon.test.ts` has no reference to the sheet, PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 47, no GameEffect, no four-sites, canon §2's one-ladder rule is respected because every axis is a raw stat point and the derived pool/a-swing strings stay where they are). Ship the FOUR unit axes now, because those are confirmed, discriminating and exactly what he described. Take the two extra axes back to him with the numbers rather than a recommendation: tell him RANGE is 35 for every boss and every tier-3 unit, tell him the bat out-accelerates Vlad, and let him choose between ATTACK SPEED with its two liars named, RANGE with its three, or four axes alone. That is a one-sentence question with the case constructed, which is what this project's rulings section asks for — and it is cheaper than building six axes twice.
